findings.finding: The node now has no open questions, records a decided design decision, and includes non-empty acceptance-criteria scenarios, falsifiability conditions, and constraints.
The node no longer leaves the umbrella lifecycle work as a catch-all bucket; it identifies the remaining migration work as follow-up child streams instead.
The remaining lifecycle debt is explicitly separated into screen-surface migration and widget-owned refresh/lane-ownership follow-up streams via child nodes.

The design incorporates the recent Pages execution-lane work by preserving a separate lifecycle track for lane-aware IPC ownership rather than collapsing all remaining debt into generic screen cleanup.
The current repo scan is distilled into concrete child streams instead of an undifferentiated backlog.
Screen migration and widget-owned refresh/lane-ownership work are no longer mixed together without ownership boundaries.
The migration split explicitly respects the newer IPC lane-isolation pattern rather than assuming a single shared-bridge lifecycle model.
The design closes the parent implementation bucket instead of reopening `screen-lifecycle` as a generic bucket for every remaining concern.
Auxiliary-lane follow-up remains explicit and subordinate to the shared control-lane model.
Previously landed cleanup work in Dashboard, Exploration, MeshDeviceDetail, and NodeInfoPanel is preserved as completed context rather than being reopened without new evidence.
The child-node split creates independently assessable follow-up units rather than another oversized migration umbrella.
